title: Choose this day (Joshua 24:15)
hook: "as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD"

segments.voice: Yesterday, the altar by the Jordan that nearly started a war. Your line was talk before you fight. Did you ask your question first? Today, Joshua's last gathering, and a choice. Day seven hundred nine.

Joshua's farewell begins with an awkward piece of family history. All the tribes are gathered at Shechem, elders, heads, judges, officers. And the story he tells starts further back than anyone might expect, before Abraham. Your fathers, he says, Terah, the father of Abraham, lived beyond the River, and served other gods. The people's history doesn't begin with faith. It begins with a man taken out of one life and led into another. Joshua tells it all, up to this moment. Then he stops, and asks the whole people to decide.
screen: `ALL THE TRIBES AT SHECHEM.` → `TERAH SERVED OTHER GODS.` → `THEN JOSHUA ASKS THEM TO DECIDE.`

segments.voice: For most of the speech, Joshua speaks in God's voice. I took your father Abraham. I sent Moses and Aaron. I brought you out. I gave you a land you didn't labor for, cities you didn't build, vineyards and olive groves you didn't plant. Everything they have arrives as a gift. Then Joshua speaks in his own voice. He urges them to serve the Lord and put away the other gods. And then, strangely, he hands them the choice anyway: if serving the Lord seems wrong to you, "choose you this day whom ye will serve." The gods your ancestors served beyond the River, or the gods of the land you live in now. And then he says where he stands: "but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD." The people answer at once: far be it from us to forsake the Lord. Then Joshua pushes back. You can't serve the Lord, he says; he is a holy God. It sounds like he's trying to talk them out of it. Some readers hear a test: a choice made too quickly is easy to drop, so he makes them choose again, slowly. They do. No, they say, we will serve the Lord. Then you are witnesses against yourselves, he tells them, and they reply in one breath: we are witnesses. So a choice gets a date and a place. Joshua writes the words in a book, and sets up a great stone under the oak at Shechem, saying the stone has heard everything. Soon after, Joshua dies, and the book draws to a close. The choice isn't made once, for all time, by a leader. Each generation stands at its own Shechem.
screen: `I TOOK, I SENT, I GAVE: ALL OF IT A GIFT.` · `CHOOSE YOU THIS DAY.` · `YOU CAN'T: CHOOSE AGAIN, SLOWLY.` · then, large: `AS FOR ME AND MY HOUSE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: decide one thing for your household. Your house might be a family, a roommate, a partner, or just you and a kettle. Let one small question come up that keeps getting put off: when you eat together, how you speak when you're tired, what happens on the day of rest, who you call each week. Don't decide everything. Choose one thing, and say it inside, in Joshua's shape: as for me and my house, we will. Finish the sentence. The bell holds the time.
Choose this day. Joshua's last words at Shechem: here are the options, here is where I stand, now you decide, and decide again. Today's word.
Your line: choose this day. Today, tell one person in your house the thing you decided, so it has a witness. Day seven hundred nine.

howItsDone: Jews read Joshua 24, the covenant at Shechem and the death of Joshua, as the close of the book of Joshua; the chapter's retelling of history, starting with Terah, is studied alongside other passages where the people's story is told aloud.

trapdoor: what you thought: a leader simply ordering people what to believe.
what it means: Joshua urges, then hands them the choice, says where he stands, and pushes back when they agree too fast.
what a scholar hears: Joshua 24:2–13 is told in God's voice: I took, I sent, I gave; the choice comes only after the gift.

notes: Auditor: teach said Joshua 'doesn't tell them what to choose'; Joshua 24:14 has him urge them to fear and serve the LORD and put away the other gods before 24:15 offers the choice. Teach and trapdoor corrected.
Joshua 24:15 is quoted from the KJV; JPS 1917 is believed to read the same in these two phrases, but please confirm and switch the citation if so.
'Some readers hear a test' for 24:19 is offered as one reading; a Keeper may add the rabbinic readings.
Joshua's age at death (24:29) is left out.
Editor: hook's 'family secret' (Terah is not a secret in the text) changed to 'an awkward piece of family history'; stock 'here is the surprise' cut; practice opener varied.
